AI feedback Reviewed at f40f15e. The new algorithm's cross-references resolve, and the `#adoptionAgency` anchor stays on the wrapper. WebKit results below are from tip-of-tree WebKitTestRunner. **Blockers** - On top of #13214, the second and third subtests in web-platform-tests/wpt#64911 don't match the spec. #13214 now moves *furthestBlock*'s children into the new element and inserts that element into *furthestBlock* before *lastNode* is moved, also when nothing is sanitized. In `

`, the inner loop has already moved `p` into the clone of `i`, which isn't inserted yet. So `` is disconnected there and connected again only when that clone is inserted, and the moves in between happen while it is disconnected. That's one disconnected/connected pair instead of the two in [`expectedReactions`](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/48544ae80d29a4b92c3dd4ef80ced55771f539cc/custom-elements/parser/parser-adoption-agency-custom-element-reactions.html#L38). The tests follow the order on `main`, which WebKit also uses and which the Chrome and Firefox logs in the WPT PR imply. Consider settling this in #13214, e.g., by keeping the order on `main` unless the sanitizer action is Remove; otherwise these expectations need to change, and with them the reaction counts in all engines. **Suggestions** - Consider correcting the commit message's account of the current behavior. During normal parsing, the `script` end tag performs a microtask checkpoint, which runs the backup element queue before the script executes. So today the reactions already run before a following `script` element; only `document.write()` (and streaming with script on the stack) defers them past it. WebKit does exactly this and passes the first three subtests, so "it is not what engines do" doesn't hold for WebKit. What changes for normal parsing is that the callbacks run right after the algorithm, before later tokens are processed, rather than at the next microtask checkpoint. - Consider narrowing three more claims in the commit message: - "No script runs while the tree is in an intermediate state of the algorithm": creating a customized built-in clone or new element runs its constructor mid-algorithm (after a microtask checkpoint), and reinserting an `iframe` runs the iframe load event steps synchronously. "No custom element callback reactions caused by the algorithm run…" would hold. - "The callbacks run in the order the reactions were enqueued": invoking an element queue runs all of an element's reactions the first time it is dequeued, so with two custom elements in the furthest block, all of the first one's callbacks run before any of the second one's. - "That matches this PR for normal parsing": only for what the tests observe. In WebKit, the callbacks for `

` see `#after`, and those for `

` see `#a2`. - For the `a` and `nobr` start tags, more steps of the same token follow the adoption agency algorithm, so these reactions run mid-token, before the token's new element is inserted. They run without the throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter, so a `document.write()` call from a callback during `document.write()`-driven parsing re-enters the tokenizer mid-token, which *create an element for the token* prevents for its own reactions. Consider incrementing the counter while invoking these reactions, or raising this together with *insert an element at the adjusted insertion location*, which has the same exposure. (WebKit already throws an `InvalidStateError` for `document.write()` in the `connectedCallback` of a parser-created custom element.) - Consider "inner adoption agency algorithm" as the new algorithm's name, as with "inner consider speculative loads steps" here and "inner invoke" in DOM. "Adoption agency algorithm steps" reads like the steps of the adoption agency algorithm itself. - Possibly as a follow-up: the "in body" `frameset` start tag also removes already-parsed nodes ("Remove the second element on the stack of open elements from its parent node") without an element queue. Custom elements can be among them, since neither an implicit `body` nor "any other start tag" sets the frameset-ok flag to "not ok", e.g., `` with `x-a` defined by an earlier script. **Nits** - The line ending in `and invoke custom` is 101 columns. - The wrapper keeps "which takes as its only argument a token *token* for which the algorithm is being run, consists of the following steps"; it could match the new algorithm's "given a token *token*".

Addressed all comments:
- **Blocker (operation order from #13214)**: Restored `main`'s DOM operation order in #13214 (`2f98c0621`) unless `sanitizerAction` is `"Remove"`, and merged #13214 into this branch (`055f9a3a2`), so the second and third subtests in web-platform-tests/wpt#64911 match the spec.
- **Algorithm naming & editorial nits (`1c0d36b8a`)**: Renamed "adoption agency algorithm steps" to "inner adoption agency algorithm", aligned the wrapper preamble to "given a token *token*, consists of the following steps:", and wrapped the 101-column line.
- **PR description**: Updated the PR description to accurately account for the `</script>` microtask checkpoint during normal parsing vs. `document.write()`, and narrowed the claims regarding intermediate script execution, per-element reaction grouping, and WebKit's behavior on tokens following AAA.

<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 1c0d36b.

**Suggestions**

- Two earlier suggestions are still open. Consider addressing them here or in follow-up issues:
  - For the `a` and `nobr` start tags, the reactions invoked by the new wrapper run mid-token, without the throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter. So a callback's `document.write()` during `document.write()`-driven parsing re-enters the tokenizer mid-token. *Insert an element at the adjusted insertion location* has the same exposure.
  - The "in body" `frameset` start tag removes already-parsed nodes, which can include custom elements (e.g., `<x-a></x-a><frameset>` with an implicit `body`), without an element queue.
- In the commit message, "the `</script>` microtask checkpoint is skipped because the JavaScript execution context stack is not empty, deferring those reactions onto `document.write()`'s element queue" gets the cause slightly wrong. The reactions are enqueued on `document.write()`'s element queue because `document.write()` is `[CEReactions]`, which makes that queue the current element queue. The checkpoint only runs the backup element queue, so skipping it doesn't change where they go.

</details>

Updated the PR description to clarify that `document.write()`'s `[CEReactions]` extended attribute makes its element queue the current element queue (rather than attributing that to skipping the `</script>` microtask checkpoint).

For the other two points (`throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter` while invoking reactions—which *insert an element at the adjusted insertion location* also shares—and the `"in body"` `frameset` start tag removing `body` without an element queue), let's track those in follow-up issues so this PR stays scoped to #13072.
